newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU monetary committee to meet on budget deficits.
newsitem.headline: EU monetary committee to meet on budget deficits.

text.p: An examination of budget policies within the European Union will top the agenda when the EU's monetary committee meets on Tuesday, monetary sources said on Monday.

The annual exercise, known as the excessive deficits procedure, will single out those governments with 1996 deficits above three percent of Gross Domestic Product -- the Maastricht limit for monetary union.
Denmark, Finland, the Netherlands, Ireland and Luxembourg are all expected to be taken off the list of fiscal offenders, with 1996 deficits at or below the Maastricht threshold.
This would mark a slight improvement over the situation in 1995 when only Denmark, Ireland and Luxembourg qualified.

Governments with excessive deficits have to demonstrate how they plan to improve their budget imbalances, a process that will be streamlined under the agreed Stability and Growth Pact for those joining a single currency.
The EU committee, comprising national treasury and central bank officials, will also review the economic convergence programmes of Spain and Portugal, sources said.

Both have made considerable progress towards meeting the Maastricht criteria, in particular Portugal, seen by many analysts as the best placed among southern European countries to join the first wave of EMU participants.
There will also be a review of European Commission economic and budget forecasts for the 15-nation bloc, due for release on April 23.
